title: Agmatine ameliorates sepsis-related intestinal injury via the AhR-STAT3-IL-10 pathway.
authors: Pan, Junhua; Gan, Lianfang; Chen, Yaying; Zhong, Lifan; Deng, Huiming; Huang, Ling; Liang, Huaping
one_liner_zh: 该文研究胍丁胺通过AhR-STAT3-IL-10通路改善脓毒症肠损伤，属纯湿实验与信号通路机制研究，无蛋白质-DNA互作建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Sepsis-related intestinal injury is essential in multi-organ dysfunction induced by the systemic inflammatory response. Agmatine (AGM) has anti-inflammatory, antioxidative, and immunomodulatory properties. However, no reports of AGM alleviating sepsis-related intestinal injury have been found. Therefore, this study intends to investigate the protective effects of AGM on sepsis-related intestinal injury and its potential mechanism. METHODS: We first established a sepsis model by lipopolysaccharide (LPS) or cecum ligation perforation (CLP), and then used H&E staining, transmission electron microscopy (TEM), and TUNEL to examine the pathological changes in rat intestines after AGM treatment. ELISA was used to detect expression levels of inflammatory factors in ileal tissues and biochemical indexes of infectionin in serum. TNF-alpha induced Caco-2 cell inflammation model was established in vitro, and cell activity and proliferative capacity were detected by CCK8 and EdU after AGM treatment. The Caco-2 cell inflammation model with high or low expression of Aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) was established, and whether AGM exerts anti-inflammatory effects via AhR/STAT3/IL-10 pathway was investigated using molecular docking, Co-IP, and Western Blot. RESULTS: The histopathological staining demonstrated that AGM significantly reduced intestinal injury and the content of inflammatory factors IL-1beta, IL-6, and TNF-alpha, improved systemic infection and the survival rate of septic mice, and restored intestinal barrier function in CLP rats. In vitro, AGM improved cell viability and proliferative capacity of the Caco-2 cell inflammation model. AGM inhibits inflammatory factor expression by activating AhR, decreasing HIF-1 protein expression, and activating the STAT3/IL-10 signaling pathway. DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSION: AGM has the potential to ameliorate sepsis-related intestinal injury via the AhR-STAT3-IL-10 pathway, thereby offering theoretical basis for clinical treatment of sepsis.
abstract_zh: 背景：脓毒症相关肠道损伤在全身炎症反应诱导的多器官功能障碍中至关重要。胍丁胺（Agmatine, AGM）具有抗炎、抗氧化和免疫调节特性。然而，尚未发现AGM缓解脓毒症相关肠道损伤的报道。因此，本研究旨在探讨AGM对脓毒症相关肠道损伤的保护作用及其潜在机制。方法：我们首先通过脂多糖（lipopolysaccharide, LPS）或盲肠结扎穿孔（cecum ligation perforation, CLP）建立脓毒症模型，然后使用H&E染色、透射电子显微镜（transmission electron microscopy, TEM）和TUNEL检测AGM处理后大鼠肠道的病理变化。ELISA用于检测回肠组织中炎症因子表达水平及血清中感染生化指标。体外建立TNF-α诱导的Caco-2细胞炎症模型，并在AGM处理后通过CCK8和EdU检测细胞活性和增殖能力。建立芳烃受体（Aryl hydrocarbon receptor, AhR）高表达或低表达的Caco-2细胞炎症模型，并通过分子对接、Co-IP和Western Blot研究AGM是否通过AhR/STAT3/IL-10通路发挥抗炎作用。结果：组织病理学染色表明，AGM显著减轻肠道损伤及炎症因子IL-1β、IL-6和TNF-α的含量，改善全身感染及脓毒症小鼠的存活率，并恢复CLP大鼠的肠道屏障功能。体外实验中，AGM改善了Caco-2细胞炎症模型的细胞活力和增殖能力。AGM通过激活AhR、降低HIF-1蛋白表达并激活STAT3/IL-10信号通路来抑制炎症因子表达。讨论与结论：AGM具有通过AhR-STAT3-IL-10通路改善脓毒症相关肠道损伤的潜力，从而为脓毒症的临床治疗提供理论基础。
